reading: Segmentation is not the bottleneck; scan visibility and the volume step are. On the 141 items / 20 scans that have lift labels, foodscan's median item APE is 50% with GT labels and 54% with lift labels (segmentation adds almost nothing); per-dish totals 30% vs 31%. The noise-free GT surface (gt_top, oracle container pose) still gives 32% median / +28% bias on the same items.

Note: after the foodscan fix (Support.height_map_volume hole-fills and rasterises the footprint at 0.5 mm) the per-item median APE with GT labels moved from 49% to ~54%: the old estimator over-counted sparse items by accident, which partly cancelled under-seeing; occlusion dominates either way.

With GT labels (ok scans, n=177): median APE / median bias foodscan 53% / -40%, voxel 46% / -26%, hull 40% / +5% (mean APE 254%: the hull blows up on non-convex items), flat-table 40% / -18%. 13% of items are missing (<20 points) and 0% non-positive.

Where it fails 1, occlusion: items hidden >= 70% in the scan (n=98) come out -57% (median bias) with GT labels, yet the same items from the full GT surface give 31% APE: the integral is fine, the visible-only cloud has no height to integrate (column fill sums observed cells only, no completion).

Where it fails 2, stacking and voids: even from noise-free surfaces the container-relative column fill over-counts, +24% median bias in stacked scans (n=62) vs +16% in unstacked ones (n=115); an item sitting on another is charged for the item below, and loose piles / leaves / toppings are charged for their air gaps (gt_top median bias by kind: topping +261%, leaves +1448%, pile +14%, piece +8%).

By size (GT labels, foodscan): <10 mL median APE 77% (bias -35%), 10-50 mL 52%, >50 mL 40% (bias -39%): large items are the ones under-seen, small ones carry the 2 mm cell footprint bias (tests: +13% on a 1 cm cylinder, +4% on 3 cm) and the hull's +8% bias.

Registration: template ICP lands 3.7 mm median from the true pose but fails (>= 10 mm) on the sparse scans (31 of 177 ok items; run_meal's init is the centroid of all off-plane points, no multi-start, no fitness gate). Replacing ICP by the true pose changes the median APE only 53% -> 59%, so for these scans occlusion, not registration, is what hurts.

run_meal's item_volume crops the whole mesh by the item's bounding box, not by label; emulated on points (foodscan_bbox) the median APE goes 53% -> 41% (bias -40% -> -5%) because neighbours, cutlery and other items inside the box are integrated too.

Dish totals (what Nutrition5k-style scoring sees), foodscan: volume median APE 30% (bias -30%, n=20 dishes) with GT labels, 30% vs 31% GT vs lift labels on the 20 lift scans; under-seeing and over-counting partly cancel in the sum, so dish error is lower than item error. Mass with oracle density, 20 dishes with complete mass labels (volume APE 30% on them): 30% with the oracle category-median density, 30% with the oracle per-item density. Densities here are oracle, never predicted; mass_g is integer-rounded for small items.

Fix first: (1) get the hidden volume (shape completion / footprint-and-height prior per item, or more views) because visible-only height maps lose 90%+ on occluded items; (2) make stacked and loose items volume-consistent (subtract the supporting item's top, solid-fill factor for piles; compute dish totals as one union column map to avoid double counting); (3) crop by label instead of bbox in run_meal.item_volume; (4) give ContainerTemplate.register a container-label init and a fitness gate so failed registrations are flagged instead of silently used.
